title: What’s Not Said Still Hurts: A Description-Based Evaluation Framework for Measuring Social Bias in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating response variations in multiple-choice and semi-generation tasks across parallel instances with different implicit/explicit age descriptors (e.g., 'college freshman' vs. 'grandmother') linked to subtly framed bias concepts.

Evaluating response variations in multiple-choice and semi-generation tasks across parallel instances with different implicit/explicit gender descriptors (e.g., family roles or gendered professions) linked to subtly framed bias concepts.

Evaluating response variations in multiple-choice and semi-generation tasks across parallel instances with different implicit/explicit racial and ethnic descriptors (e.g., culturally specific names, pet phrases, or holidays) linked to subtly framed bias concepts.

Evaluating response variations in multiple-choice and semi-generation tasks across parallel instances with different implicit/explicit socioeconomic descriptors (e.g., descriptions of wealth or living conditions) linked to subtly framed bias concepts.

Evaluating response variations in multiple-choice and semi-generation tasks across parallel instances with different implicit/explicit religious descriptors (e.g., religious practices, behaviors, or attire) linked to subtly framed bias concepts.
